title: The same data can lead to different endpoints
K-means favors compact Euclidean groups
The objective alone cannot choose K
notes: Splitting a cluster cannot increase the globally optimal squared-error objective. If every observation has its own center, distortion is zero. That does not make n clusters useful.

notes: This deck uses ordinary Euclidean distances, the standard default. The source writes squared distances; that is a different dissimilarity choice and produces different numerical scores. When both a and b are zero, use zero.

title: Replace one-hot assignments with responsibilities
A Gaussian needs a mean and a covariance
notes: A covariance is generally positive semidefinite; an invertible covariance is required by the standard nonsingular Gaussian density. Regularization prevents singular fitted components.

title: Mix densities with nonnegative weights
Normalize each component’s weighted density
Maximize the observed-data log likelihood
Use the current model to improve the next one
notes: Corrects wording that suggests taking an expectation of likelihood rather than log likelihood. Exact EM has a nondecreasing observed likelihood, but not a global-optimum guarantee.

title: The M-step is a soft version of averaging
Watch EM reshape three Gaussian components
notes: Added full-covariance, three-component EM on all original 240 points. Forty updates; diagonal covariance regularization 10⁻⁶. Ellipses are one Mahalanobis-radius contours, not 68% regions in 2D. Soft probabilities update for the chosen point.

title: A rising likelihood still needs interpretation
K-means is related to a limiting mixture model
notes: Ordinary Lloyd K-means is not literally unrestricted Gaussian-mixture EM. Describe it as a hard-assignment or small-variance connection rather than conflating the two algorithms.

The linkage rule changes the tree
notes: Average linkage weights each observation pair equally. It is not the same as equally averaging distances between merged clusters regardless of their sizes.

title: Keep d directions, then map back approximately
notes: Ud has orthonormal columns. Explained variance is not predictive accuracy or evidence that discarded directions are irrelevant to a downstream task.

title: Rescaling does not make a feature Gaussian
notes: Standardization does not turn an arbitrary distribution into a normal distribution. New observations can lie outside a fitted min–max range. Sample vs population variance conventions must be stated.

title: Compare every original preprocessing panel

title: Identity covariance comes at a price
notes: The identity assumes positive retained eigenvalues and a consistent covariance convention. A truncated transform whitens only the retained subspace.
